verdict.line: You lose if he catches mini Gnar inside his W/E all-in before you can transform; you win if you survive to Mega Gnar and a finished Trinity Force, where he has no answer left.

brief.thesis: Renekton's full combo — Ruthless Predator's double or triple slash stun chained into Slice and Dice's gap-close — only threatens you while you're mini Gnar and squishy, which is exactly why he holds the solo-kill edge despite the lane grading even. Your 1100-range Q lets you poke him down without ever entering his 300-325 unit kill box. The 47.7% win rate over 220 games reflects a lane where trades are balanced but his all-in timing is the whole threat; once Rage gives you Mega Gnar and Trinity Force comes online, the math swings back to you.

theirWindow.when: Fury above 50 with W and E up
theirWindow.what: He gets a 3-hit Ruthless Predator that strips shields and stuns for 1.5s, chained off a free Slice and Dice gap-close. Disengage to max Q range and let the window pass rather than trading face to face.

yourWindow.when: You're Mega Gnar, his W/E on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Mega Gnar's W stomp stuns him in place and E's landing deals area damage with no bounce needed. Initiate now instead of waiting for him to rebuild Fury and reset his engage tools.

start.why: Run with the 66.7%-pick, 47.7%-win-rate start; the extra HP and sustain buy you room to survive his early poke while you're still mini Gnar and can't out-trade him in melee.

boots.why: 89.7% pick for a reason — Renekton's entire kit (Q, W, auto-attack Fury generation) is physical, so the flat reduction directly blunts his all-in damage.

core.why: This is the spike that flips the lane; once it's up you out-duel his Dominus form instead of just surviving it.
Armor shred keeps your Q/auto trades relevant as he stacks HP through Tyrant form and lets you punish his lowered-armor E dash in kind.
71% win rate on this path over 31 games — the shield answers his burst-stun combo directly and keeps you alive through the one window he actually threatens you in.

he's stacking magic resist or the fight is dragging into extended skirmishes where attack speed outvalues burst

runes.keystoneWhy: The move speed on heal/mana restore directly serves OP.GG's own call to manage distance as mini Gnar — you proc it by poking with Q, not by standing in his stun range. Master-tier Gnar players instead run Lethal Tempo across 1,803 games for a higher measured 57.6% win rate; that fits a more aggressive, stand-and-kite playstyle once you're confident trading autos through his Fury window.

summoners.why: Teleport is the 62.3%-pick standard and lets you scale into the split-push and Trinity Force power spike this matchup rewards. Flash+Ignite actually posts the higher measured win rate (53.2% over 17.7% pick) if you'd rather punish his all-in attempts directly and end the lane in kills instead of outscaling it.

playing.title: Poke, don't melee
playing.detail: Use Q at its full 1100 range to chip his HP and force Fury off cooldown timing. Never trade inside his 300-325 unit range before you're Mega Gnar.

playing.title: Back off above 50 Fury
playing.detail: Once his bar crosses half, Q's heal doubles and W becomes a 3-hit, shield-destroying 1.5s stun. Disengage rather than contest a trade in that window.

playing.title: Hold E to punish his dash
playing.detail: Save Hop to reposition the instant he commits Slice and Dice at you, rather than burning it just to poke — its 22-12s cooldown by rank is too valuable to waste.

playing.title: Fight only as Mega Gnar
playing.detail: Wait for Rage to transform you before contesting any trade. Mega Gnar's W stomp stun and added bulk directly answer his W/E stun chain.

playing.title: Land R into walls
playing.detail: In skirmishes, aim GNAR! to throw him into terrain for the bonus-damage stun — his Dominus has only 20 range, so he can't threaten you back at the distance R creates.

playing.title: Trade right after Bone Plating procs
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to fight once Bone Plating has absorbed his burst. Initiate in the 1-2s after it triggers, not before.

playing.title: Rush Trinity Force, not side items
playing.detail: Every later item (Black Cleaver, Sterak's) depends on Trinity being first; delaying it extends the window where he still has the edge.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/pick-rate numbers are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.20.1) — nothing here is estimated. The ability breakdowns, timing windows, and tactical reasoning are my own read of the matchup, built to explain why those numbers land where they do.

stats.opponentTip: He is difficult to defeat head on, so manage your distance when you are Mini Gnar and use [R] when Mega Gnar. Try fighting him when you have Bone Plating.
